function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • A single pane of glass that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards that surface performance, cost, and capacity across all workloads. | Unilever can see the health of its global supply‑chain, marketing, and e‑commerce workloads in one place, eliminating the “cloud‑silos” problem. | | **AI‑Driven Root‑Cause Analysis** | • Machine‑learning models that automatically correlate events, logs, and metrics to pinpoint the source of latency, errors, or cost spikes.
• Predictive alerts before problems become outages. | Faster incident response means less downtime for Unilever’s retail platforms and fewer lost sales. | | **Dynamic Capacity & Cost Optimization** | • Continuous optimization engine that recommends right‑sizeing, auto‑scaling, and spot‑instance usage based on real‑time demand.
• Automated policy enforcement (e.g., “no more than 10 % over‑provisioned”). | Unilever can keep cloud spend under control while ensuring performance for high‑traffic campaigns. | | **Policy‑Based Governance** | • Declarative policies that span multiple clouds (e.g., “All workloads must run on at least one spot instance”).
• Auditable compliance reports. | Simplifies governance across the organization’s diverse cloud portfolio. | | **Self‑Healing & Auto‑Remediation** | • AI models that trigger automated remediation actions (restart, scale, migrate) when thresholds are breached.
• Integration with CI/CD pipelines for rapid rollbacks. | Reduces manual toil for Unilever’s DevOps teams and keeps services highly available. | | **Unified Cost Allocation & Chargeback** | • Tag‑based cost attribution that maps spend to business units, product lines, or projects.
• Forecasting and budgeting tools. | Enables Unilever to allocate cloud spend accurately to marketing, R&D, and operations budgets. | #### How It Works in Practice 1. **Data Ingestion** – Turbonomics pulls telemetry from CloudWatch, Stackdriver, Azure Monitor, Prometheus, and custom agents on VMs/containers. 2. **AI Engine** – Uses supervised and unsupervised learning to detect anomalies, predict future load, and recommend optimizations. 3. **Action Layer** – Executes API calls to the respective cloud providers (or Kubernetes APIs) to scale, migrate, or shut down resources. 4. **Reporting** – Generates dashboards, alerts, and compliance reports that can be embedded into existing BI tools. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Observability Tools | Feature | Turbonomics | GCP Operations (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch | Azure Monitor | |---------|-------------|---------------------------------------|----------------|---------------| | **Scope** | Multi‑cloud + on‑prem + edge | Single‑cloud (GCP) | Single‑cloud (AWS) | Single‑cloud (Azure) | | **Unified Dashboard** | One UI for all clouds | Separate dashboards per cloud | Separate dashboards per cloud | Separate dashboards per cloud | | **AI/ML Capabilities** | Built‑in ML for root‑cause, predictive scaling, cost forecasting | Basic anomaly detection, limited ML | Basic anomaly detection, limited ML | Basic anomaly detection, limited ML | | **Cost Optimization** | Continuous, policy‑driven optimization across clouds | Cost Explorer (reports only) | Cost Explorer (reports only) | Cost Management (reports only) | | **Auto‑Remediation** | Automated remediation via API calls | Manual alarms + Lambda/Functions | Manual alarms + Lambda/Functions | Manual alerts + Logic Apps | | **Governance & Policy** | Declarative policies spanning clouds | IAM policies per service | IAM policies per service | RBAC + Policy definitions per resource | | **Integration** | Native APIs for all clouds + Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible | GCP APIs only | AWS APIs only | Azure APIs only | | **Chargeback & Allocation** | Tag‑based, multi‑dimensional reporting | Billing reports, budgets | Billing reports, budgets | Billing reports, budgets | | **Learning Curve** | Requires learning Turbonomics UI & APIs | Familiar to GCP users | Familiar to AWS users | Familiar to Azure users | | **Cost** | Subscription fee (depends on size) | Included in cloud usage | Included in cloud usage | Included in cloud usage | #### Key Takeaways - **Single Pane of Glass** – Turbonomics eliminates the need to switch between GCP, AWS, Azure consoles. - **Cross‑Cloud AI** – Native tools provide basic anomaly detection; Turbonomics offers advanced ML that spans all environments. - **Automation & Governance** – Turbonomics automates remediation and enforces policies across clouds, whereas native tools require manual scripting or separate services. - **Cost Control** – Turbonomics continuously optimizes spend; native tools mainly provide reporting and budgeting. --- ### Bottom Line for Unilever By adopting Turbonomics, Unilever can: 1. **Reduce Operational Complexity** – One platform for monitoring, optimization, and governance across all its cloud deployments. 2. **Accelerate Innovation** – AI‑driven insights free up engineering teams to focus on product features rather than infrastructure maintenance. 3. **Control Costs** – Continuous optimization and chargeback enable tighter budget adherence across marketing, supply chain, and digital commerce. 4. **Ensure Compliance** – Policy enforcement and audit trails help meet regulatory requirements in different regions. In contrast, relying solely on native GCP, AWS, or Azure observability tools would mean maintaining separate dashboards, writing custom scripts for cross‑cloud automation, and missing out on the AI‑powered optimization that Turbonomics brings to the table.
